# source: conformance/scenarios/edge.txt

scenario edge/lone-slash
kind git-quirk
spec A pattern consisting only of a slash is not described by gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| /
path a => NONE
path a/ => NONE
path a/b => NONE

scenario edge/double-slash-pattern
kind git-quirk
spec A pattern consisting only of slashes is not described by gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| //
| ///
path a => NONE
path a/ => NONE
path a/b => NONE

scenario edge/leading-double-slash
kind git-quirk
spec A leading slash anchors the pattern.
note Two leading slashes are not collapsed.
file .gitignore
| //foo
path foo => NONE
path a/foo => NONE
path foo/ => NONE

scenario edge/bang-alone
kind git-quirk
spec A lone exclamation mark negates an empty pattern.
file .gitignore
| *
| !
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*

scenario edge/bang-slash
kind git-quirk
spec A negated pattern consisting of a slash is not described by gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| *
| !/
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*

scenario edge/slash-star-star
kind normative
spec A lone "/**" matches everything inside the directory of the ignore file.
file .gitignore
| /**
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:/**
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:/**
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:/**

scenario edge/star-slash-star-star
kind normative
spec A trailing "/**" matches everything inside.
file .gitignore
| */**
path a => NONE
path a/ => NONE
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*/**
path a/b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*/**
path b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*/**

scenario edge/double-star-slash-only
kind git-quirk
spec A leading "**" followed by a slash means match in all directories.
file .gitignore
| **/
path a => NONE
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/
path a/b/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/
path a/b/c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/

scenario edge/double-star-slash-double-star
kind git-quirk
spec A pattern made of "**/**" is not described by gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| **/**
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/**
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/**
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/**

scenario edge/dot-and-dotdot-patterns
kind git-quirk
spec Patterns are compared literally.
file .gitignore
| .
| ..
| ...
path .hidden => NONE
path ... => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:...
path a/... => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:...

scenario edge/dot-directories-and-files
kind normative
spec A dot at the start of a name is an ordinary character for matching purposes.
file .gitignore
| *
| !.gitignore
| .*
path .hidden => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:.*
path .gitignore => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:.*
path sub/.hidden => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*
path visible => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*

scenario edge/very-long-name
kind normative
spec Patterns and names have no special length limit in gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa*b
path aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa*b
path aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaac => NONE

scenario edge/many-stars-backtracking
kind normative
spec An asterisk matches anything except a slash, with any number of asterisks.
file .gitignore
| *a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b
path aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaac => NONE
path aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b
path aaaaaaaab => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b
path aaaaaaab => NONE

scenario edge/deep-path
kind normative
spec A pattern without a slash matches at any level below the ignore file.
file .gitignore
| leaf
| deep/**/end
path a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h/i/j/leaf => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:leaf
path a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h/i/j/leafy => NONE
path deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h/i/j/end => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:deep/**/end
path deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g/h/i/j/ends => NONE

scenario edge/ignored-parent-with-deep-negation-in-same-file
kind normative
spec It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded.
file .gitignore
| a/
| !a/b/
| !a/b/c.txt
path a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/
path a/b/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/
path a/b/c.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/
path x/a/b/c.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a/

scenario edge/later-negation-without-slash-covers-directories
kind normative
spec Within one file the last matching pattern decides, so a later negation without a slash re-includes both files and directories.
file .gitignore
| out/
| !out
path out => INCLUDED # .gitignore:2:!out
path out/ => INCLUDED # .gitignore:2:!out
path a/out => INCLUDED # .gitignore:2:!out

scenario edge/pattern-matching-gitdir-name
kind normative
spec A .git directory is not special to the pattern syntax.
file .gitignore
| .git
| .gitmodules
path .gitmodules => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:.gitmodules
path sub/.gitmodules => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:.gitmodules
path other => NONE

scenario edge/escape-at-start-of-pattern
kind normative
spec A backslash before a character that needs no escaping stands for that character.
file .gitignore
| \a
| \*b
| \?c
path a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:\a
path *b => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:\*b
path xb => NONE
path ?c => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:\?c
path xc => NONE

scenario edge/bracket-with-slash
kind git-quirk
spec Wildcards in git match with the pathname flag, so a slash cannot be matched by a bracket expression.
file .gitignore
| a[/]b
| c[a/]d
path a/b => NONE
path ab => NONE
path c/d => NONE
path cad => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c[a/]d

scenario edge/empty-brackets
kind git-quirk
spec Behavior of an empty bracket expression is not described by gitignore(5).
file .gitignore
| a[]b
| c[!]d
| e[^]f
path a[]b => NONE
path ab => NONE
path c[!]d => NONE
path cd => NONE
path e[^]f => NONE

scenario edge/bracket-containing-star
kind normative
spec Special characters lose their meaning inside a bracket expression.
file .gitignore
| a[*?]b
path a*b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[*?]b
path a?b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[*?]b
path acb => NONE
path a[b => NONE

scenario edge/escaped-bracket-closing-pair
kind normative
spec A backslash makes the following character ordinary.
file .gitignore
| a\[b\]c
path a[b]c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a\[b\]c
path abc => NONE
path ab => NONE

scenario edge/double-star-with-negation
kind normative
spec It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded, even when the rule uses a leading "**".
file .gitignore
| **/node_modules/
| !**/node_modules/keep/
path node_modules/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/node_modules/
path a/node_modules/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/node_modules/
path node_modules/keep/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/node_modules/
path a/node_modules/keep/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/node_modules/
path node_modules/x/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:**/node_modules/

scenario edge/same-pattern-in-two-levels
kind normative
spec Patterns in lower level files override those in higher level files, including identical patterns.
file .gitignore
| !x
file d/.gitignore
| x
file d/e/.gitignore
| !x
path x => INCLUDED # .gitignore:1:!x
path d/x => IGNORED # d/.gitignore:1:x
path d/e/x => INCLUDED # d/e/.gitignore:1:!x
path d/e/f/x => INCLUDED # d/e/.gitignore:1:!x
